channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: JRNL Magazine Open Call 2026 · FotoFilmic
item.description: JRNL is FotoFilmic's recurring photography magazine. This open call (Summer/Fall 2026 issue) accepts all lens-based contemporary practices — from film and alternative or historical processes to digital and hybrid methods. Photographers submit up to 25 images from a single cohesive project or series, with work created after January 1, 2016. Selected photographers each receive 10 full spreads (20 pages) in the A4-format magazine plus a complimentary print copy; the issue launches November 13, 2026 in Paris during Paris Photo week. — Deadline: July 5, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Publication (10 spreads) + print copy.

item.title: Exposure One Awards - Photographer of the Year 2026
item.description: Annual international photography contest from Exposure One Awards honouring outstanding photographers across 20 categories — including Abstract, Architecture, Conceptual, Fine Art, Landscapes, Portrait, Street, Travel and Wildlife. Entries are accepted as single images or series of 2–5 images from film, digital or mobile devices. Over $4,000 in cash prizes, plus an artist profile, winner's gallery feature, press release and interview. Judged by an international panel drawn from SFMOMA, Aperture, Vogue, the Art Gallery of Alberta and Leica Gallery LA. — Deadline: September 2, 2026. Fee: $22–$50. Prize: $4,000+.

item.title: Blank Wall Gallery — Summer
item.description: Open call on the theme 'Summer' — a season of light, movement, heat and stillness, from sunlit days and travel to quiet moments, expressed through urban scenes, natural landscapes or personal perspectives. Free to submit; selected photographers pay a participation fee only if exhibited (€35 if the photo is printed, €15 if shown on the gallery's digital screen). Selected work is shown at Blank Wall Gallery in Athens, September 25 – October 7, 2026. — Deadline: August 14, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Reflections Through Time: 2026 Evendale Juried Photography Exhibition
item.description: A juried photography exhibition presented by the Evendale Cultural Arts Center as part of the 2026 FotoFocus Biennial, marking the Village of Evendale's 75th anniversary. The theme 'Reflections Through Time' invites work exploring memory, history, change, identity and the stories that connect past, present and future, interpreted personally or universally, documentary or conceptual. Open to amateur and professional photographers residing within a 50-mile radius of Evendale, Ohio (students 18 and under may enter a Student Division). Selected photographs are reproduced on large-scale 4-by-4-foot weatherproof panels and installed outdoors along the Village pool fence as a free public art installation (September 13 – December 31, 2026). Juried by Carolyn Teepen, Assistant Professor of Photography and Filmmaking at Thomas More University. — Deadline: August 14, 2026. Fee: $10 per image (up to 5); free for Evendale residents and students 18 and under. Prize: $1,000+ cash + Exhibition.

item.title: Color Space: Contemporary Photography 2026 · Black Box Gallery
item.description: Open call from Black Box Gallery in Portland, OR for a juried exhibition of contemporary color photography spanning landscape, portrait, architecture and conceptual work, examining how photographers use colour. 26 photographs are selected for the in-gallery exhibition (September 1–25, 2026), 50 additional photographs are featured in an online gallery annex, and all 76 selected works are reproduced in a printed Blurb catalog. Open to amateur and professional photographers worldwide. Juried by Todd Johnson (founder/director of Black Box Gallery, MFA San Francisco Art Institute). — Deadline: August 7, 2026. Fee: $40 for 5 images. Prize: Exhibition + catalog.

item.title: The Autumn National 2026 · Cape Cod Art Center
item.description: Open juried national all-media exhibition at Cape Cod Art Center in Barnstable, Massachusetts, with photography included among the accepted media. Selected work is shown in the center's galleries, with cash awards presented across categories as in the center's other National exhibitions. Open to all artists; entries submitted via Smarter Entry. — Deadline: September 20, 2026. Fee: $30/piece ($25 members). Prize: Cash awards + Exhibition.

item.title: Photography+ Open Call: Multiplication · Photoworks
item.description: Open call for the next issue of Photography+, Photoworks' online magazine, on the theme 'Multiplication' — exploring how images are reproduced and replicated in photography, with a focus on digital networks and emerging technologies. Submit a single image responding to the theme; one selected work receives an £80 artist fee and is featured in the next issue of Photography+, launching alongside the Photoworks Annual 'Multi Multi'. Open to anyone, anywhere in the world, with no professional experience required. — Deadline: September 25, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: £80 + Publication.

item.title: John Chervinsky Emerging Photographer Scholarship 2026 · Griffin Museum of Photography
item.description: Annual scholarship from the Griffin Museum of Photography honouring photographer and scientist John Chervinsky, recognising emerging photographers with the potential to build a sustained body of work and solo exhibitions. The recipient receives a $3,000 cash award, a solo exhibition at the Griffin Museum, and a volume from Chervinsky's personal library of photography books. Open to photographers without gallery representation who have not had a solo exhibition in a commercial, academic, organisational or museum gallery — coffee shops, community galleries, libraries and academic thesis shows are eligible settings — and who have not received grant funding over $3,000; those enrolled in a photography degree programme may apply only in their graduating year. Entry is free: submit ten photographs in intended viewing order along with a bio/CV, a statement of artistic purpose and a statement on the work. The submission window opens 1 October 2026 and closes 22 November 2026, with the awardee announced by January 2027. — Deadline: November 22, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $3,000 + solo exhibition at the Griffin Museum.

item.title: SE Center for Photography — The Abandoned Landscape
item.description: Virtual juried exhibition from the Southeast Center for Photography on the abandoned landscape — rural or urban, desert or jungle, ancient to recent — and the visible effects of time's passage, decay and deterioration across the places people leave behind. Colour and black-and-white work accepted in analog, digital or antique processes. 35–40 selected images are featured in an approximately month-long virtual gallery opening 15 September 2026, with social-media promotion and an archived video walkthrough. 100% of any sales go to the artist; no commission. Open to all photographers worldwide regardless of location, age or skill level. — Deadline: August 15, 2026. Fee: $35/5 images ($28 members). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: CPA International Juried Exhibition 2026 · Center for Photographic Art
item.description: Annual international juried exhibition at the Center for Photographic Art's historic gallery in Carmel-by-the-Sea, California. Forty-five photographs are selected for the gallery show (December 6, 2026 – January 3, 2027), with a further 45 in an online gallery, competing for eight cash awards totalling over $6,000 — including First Place ($2,500), Second, Third, Merit awards and the Salon Jane Award for Women in Photography. Open to all photographers 18+ worldwide working in still photographic media; any subject. Submission period July 1 – October 1, 2026. — Deadline: October 1, 2026. Fee: $65/3 images ($45 members), +$10 each additional. Prize: 8 cash awards over $6,000.

item.title: W. Eugene Smith Grant in Humanistic Photography 2026
item.description: The 46th annual grant from the W. Eugene Smith Memorial Fund (established 1979), awarded to a photographer whose past work and proposed project continue Smith's tradition of humanistic, concerned photography. The recipient receives $30,000 ($24,000 on award, $6,000 on delivery); two finalists receive $10,000 each. Open to photographers 18+ of any nationality, professional or non-professional (students apply to the separate Student Grant). Submit a bio, project description and proposal with up to 40 images. The call opens July 1, 2026. — Deadline: October 12, 2026. Fee: $50 (waivers available). Prize: $30,000 + two $10,000 finalist grants.

item.title: Through the Lens: Presence and Absence · Workshop13
item.description: Third photography-dedicated juried exhibition at ArtWorks Gallery, run by Workshop13, a nonprofit cultural arts and learning center in Ware, Massachusetts. The theme explores how what we see in a photograph is shaped by what is missing — visibility versus implication, spaces that suggest human presence, objects that stand in for memory. Selected works are shown in the gallery. AI-generated work is not accepted. — Deadline: July 6, 2026. Fee: $25 (1 image) / $35 (up to 3). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: KinoSaito Artist-in-Residence 2026
item.description: Four-week fall residency (November 8 – December 6, 2026) at KinoSaito, an arts center in a renovated former Catholic school in Verplanck, New York. Two professional artists each receive a 900 sq ft studio with loft living quarters (kitchenette and private bathroom) and a $1,500 stipend for living costs and supplies. All media are accepted, including photography and lens-based work; currently enrolled students are not eligible. — Deadline: July 5, 2026. Fee: $30 ($25 members). Prize: $1,500 stipend + studio & housing.

item.title: Pioneer Works Visual Arts Residency 2027
item.description: Open call for the 2027 cohort of Pioneer Works' Visual Arts Residency, at the major nonprofit cultural center in Red Hook, Brooklyn. Each year 12 visual-arts residents receive a one-time $5,000 award and five months of studio access, plus free use of facilities — including a darkroom, risograph, ceramics studio, large-format and 3D printers, and laser cutter — biweekly studio visits with curators and critics, and access to public programs. Photographers and lens-based artists are eligible. Applications June 15 – July 13, 2026. — Deadline: July 13, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $5,000 + 5-month studio residency.

item.title: BigCi Environmental Awards 2026
item.description: Annual environmental awards from BigCi (Bilpin international ground for Creative Initiatives), an established artist residency in Bilpin, in the UNESCO World Heritage-listed Blue Mountains of New South Wales, Australia. Two winners each receive a four-week funded residency at BigCi plus A$5,000 in prize money. Open to artists across disciplines — visual art, installation, multimedia, performance, music, photography, film and curating. Winners announced 22 August 2026. — Deadline: August 2, 2026. Fee: A$40. Prize: 4-week residency + A$5,000 (×2 winners).

item.title: Catskill Art Space Call for Submissions 2026
item.description: Catskill Art Space, a nonprofit contemporary art center in Livingston Manor, New York (a renovated 1929 theater that has presented work via Pace Gallery), invites single-artist exhibition proposals for its programme. Selected artists receive a $1,000 honorarium toward art transit and preparation and a solo presentation in a ground-floor gallery, chosen by the Artists Council. All media are welcome, including photography; artists who exhibited in the 2017–26 season are ineligible, and regional (Catskills/Upstate NY) artists are prioritized. — Deadline: July 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $1,000 honorarium + solo presentation.

item.title: Hunt Museum Open Submission Exhibition 2026
item.description: The second annual juried open submission exhibition at The Hunt Museum, a museum in Limerick, Ireland housed in the historic Custom House. It accepts painting, photography, sculpture, printmaking, drawing and mixed media (made in the past five years) from artists in Ireland and worldwide, fostering dialogue between contemporary practice and the historic collection. Selected works are exhibited 6 December 2026 – 21 February 2027 and are expected to be for sale (the museum takes 25% commission). Selection notified 17 October 2026. — Deadline: September 7, 2026. Fee: €15 per artwork (up to 3). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: SE Center for Photography — The Figure as Art
item.description: Virtual juried exhibition from the Southeast Center for Photography exploring the human figure as art — the body as form, gesture and subject. Juror Howard Schatz, the acclaimed New York fine-art photographer, selects 25–35 images for an approximately month-long virtual gallery opening 30 September 2026, with social-media promotion across SEC4P's channels and an archived online slideshow and video walkthrough. 100% of any sales go to the artist; there is no commission. Open to all photographers worldwide of any skill level; work previously exhibited at SE Center within the prior two years is ineligible. — Deadline: September 1, 2026. Fee: $35/5 images ($28 members). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Maghreb Photography Awards 2026
item.description: International photography award spotlighting contemporary work from the 'Greater Maghreb' and the wider Mediterranean basin — a region underrepresented in most awards. Entrants submit a single image or a series of 5–15 across themed categories, with one category reserved for photographers of Maghreb origin or residence and another for African projects. A $2,000 prize pool is shared across category winners, and selected work is exhibited at partner festivals including the Rendez-Vous de la photo d'Essaouira (Morocco) and events in Tunisia in autumn 2026, with press promotion. Early-bird fees (before 8 June) start at €12 for a single image; standard fees €15 single, €34–41 for a series. — Deadline: July 5, 2026. Fee: €15 single / €34–41 series (+€5 per extra category). Prize: $2,000 prize pool + festival exhibitions.

item.title: Prix Photoforum 2026 · Photoforum Pasquart
item.description: Annual open call from Photoforum Pasquart, a leading Swiss photography institution in Biel/Bienne. The jury selects between 10 and 15 photographers and artists working in photographic media to present their work in a group exhibition at Photoforum Pasquart in December 2026. All photographic practices are welcome, including documentary photography, experimental processes, installation, video and digital media. There is no set theme — applicants explore the possibilities of the photographic medium and demonstrate a distinctive approach to their practice, and submitted work must have been created within the last two years. One participant receives the Prix Photoforum of CHF 5,000, and all selected participants receive CHF 500 toward production and transport costs. — Deadline: July 7, 2026. Fee: CHF 65 (CHF 35 students/apprentices with proof; free for members). Prize: CHF 5,000.

item.title: Kyoto Retreat 2026
item.description: A fully-funded four-week retreat in Kyoto, Japan, conceived as a time for rest, research and reflection rather than production. Open to visual artists, curators and writers aged 21+ at all career stages and working in any discipline, including photography, moving image and the written word. Selected participants receive round-trip airfare to Kansai/Osaka, private accommodation in a shared house for the duration, and an $800 USD stipend for meals and local transportation. The 2026 retreat runs November 1–30, 2026. — Deadline: July 17, 2026. Fee: $95 USD application fee (non-refundable). Prize: $800 stipend.

item.title: Liu Shiming Artist Grants 2026
item.description: The fourth annual round of grants from the Liu Shiming Art Foundation supporting early-career visual artists, including photographers, in the first decade of their practice. Up to five artists are each awarded a $5,000 grant to support a current or new project that explores the interplay between traditional, cultural or historical influences and contemporary artistic practice. The application period runs June 1 – August 31, 2026, and is open to artists from any country (application materials must be in English). — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Up to five grants of $5,000 each.

item.title: PhMuseum 2026 Women Photographers Grant
item.description: Now in its 10th edition, the PhMuseum Women Photographers Grant supports the work and careers of female and non-binary photographers of all ages and from all countries, working across documentary, fine art and conceptual photography. The open call awards a total of $11,000 in cash prizes plus €5,000 in MPB gear vouchers: $5,500 (1st), $2,200 (2nd), $1,100 (3rd), a $2,200 New Generation prize for entrants aged 30 or under, and two MPB Special Mentions of €2,500 in vouchers each. Selected work is shown in a solo exhibition at PhMuseum Lab, screened at the PhotoVogue Festival, and featured via a Vogue Italia interview; every entrant also receives a 30-minute portfolio review with a PhMuseum Education mentor. The grant promotes stories told from a female and non-binary perspective and advances gender equality across the photography industry. — Deadline: October 10, 2026. Fee: €25 until Sep 19, then €30 until Oct 10. Prize: $11,000 + vouchers + Exhibition.

item.title: Solo Exhibition August 2026 · All About Photo
item.description: Monthly featured photographer showcase. Winner receives a full month online solo exhibition (August 1–31, 2026), permanent gallery presence, exclusive interview, social media promotion, newsletter feature, international press coverage, and commission-free sales. Submit a cohesive project or portfolio of 6–14 images. — Deadline: July 21, 2026. Fee: $45. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Susan McLaughlin Risograph Photobook Award 2026 · Penumbra Foundation
item.description: Award from New York's Penumbra Foundation honouring risograph-printed photobooks. Open to artists, publishers and printers worldwide for risograph photobooks made between July 2024 and July 2026, where photography gives the context of the narrative or content. Submit one physical copy of the book by mail along with a printed entry form; entry is free, with applicants covering shipping costs (international entrants declare the book as a donation with no commercial value). The winner receives a $5,000 award and is presented at Penumbra's In The Fold photobook forum, with additional online features. Books produced through the Penumbra Risograph Residency are not eligible. Juror to be announced. — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $5,000.

item.title: 2026 Lucie Photo Book Prize · Lucie Foundation
item.description: Annual photobook prize from the Lucie Foundation, awarded to photographers and publishers who have created photobook projects anywhere in the world between September 2024 and September 2026. Three cash prizes: Book of the Year ($3,000, to the publisher), First Book ($2,000, to a photographer publishing their first book) and Self-Published ($2,000, for self-published and handmade books). Eligible works include exhibition catalogues, self-published, limited edition, multi-artist, single-author, zine and reissue titles. Submit a full cover-to-cover PDF of the book with the entry form. Photographers pay $50 for the first submission; publishers $75; 20% off each additional category. — Deadline: September 15, 2026. Fee: $50 photographers / $75 publishers. Prize: $3,000 + 2×$2,000.

item.title: The Colour Library: Yellow — Shutter Hub Editions Publication
item.description: Open call for The Colour Library: Yellow, part of Shutter Hub Editions' series of photobooks exploring the emotional, symbolic and visual power of a single colour. The editors seek images in which yellow is present, dominant or symbolically charged, across all photographic styles. 100 images are selected for a perfect-bound printed book held in national archives including the British Library and the V&A. Pay-what-you-can entry with a £15 minimum; free submissions available on request for photographers with limited income. Open worldwide, up to 10 images per submission. Selected photographers receive a publication credit and a dedicated promotion page; no royalties or free copies. — Deadline: July 16, 2026. Fee: £15+. Prize: Publication in printed photobook.

item.title: 2026 Paris Photo–Aperture PhotoBook Awards
item.description: Annual photobook awards from Aperture in partnership with Paris Photo — among the most prestigious in the field. Three categories: First PhotoBook (a photographer or artist's debut book, $10,000 prize), PhotoBook of the Year, and Photography Catalog of the Year. Thirty-five books are shortlisted (20 First PhotoBook, 10 PhotoBook of the Year, 5 Catalog) and exhibited at Paris Photo at the Grand Palais in November 2026, then in a touring exhibition. Open worldwide to photographers, artists, publishers, or third parties acting with the maker's consent; submitted books must be published between September 6, 2025 and September 4, 2026. Submit online via Picter and mail a physical copy to Aperture in New York. Early-bird entry until July 10, 2026; regular rates thereafter. — Deadline: September 4, 2026. Fee: $15–$60. Prize: $10,000 (First PhotoBook) + Paris Photo exhibition.

item.title: Looking In — SaveArtSpace Billboard Exhibition
item.description: Public art exhibition on billboard advertising space in New York City, curated by Jessica Alazraki, opening September 11, 2026. Looking In explores what it means to observe from a distance — through windows, thresholds, memories, cultures, and personal experiences — and the spaces between public and private, insider and outsider, visibility and mystery. Inspired by life in a city where glimpses into a neighbor’s world are unavoidable, it reflects on how looking creates curiosity, empathy, and connection. Open to all mediums, including photography, and to artists of all ages and backgrounds. Selected works are displayed on NYC ad space for at least one month; artists are notified after August 10, 2026. SaveArtSpace is a non-profit that has placed artists’ work on commercial ad space since 2015, and fees are tax-deductible donations supporting exhibition production. — Deadline: July 27, 2026. Fee: $35 (1–3 images), $10 each additional. Prize: Billboard exhibition in NYC.

item.title: Dignity Not For Sale — SaveArtSpace Bus Shelter Exhibition
item.description: Public art exhibition on bus shelter advertising space in Miami, FL, curated by Lizzie Suarez, opening September 18, 2026. A call to celebrate the belonging, dignity, and resilience of Miami’s working class as the city is reshaped by wealth and real estate — an invitation to remember what makes Miami special and that our dignity is not for sale. Welcoming submissions of all mediums, including photography, that address these themes, from artists of all ages and backgrounds. Selected works are displayed on Miami ad space for at least one month. SaveArtSpace is a non-profit that has placed artists’ work on commercial ad space since 2015, and fees are tax-deductible donations supporting exhibition production. — Deadline: August 3, 2026. Fee: $35 (1–3 images), $10 each additional. Prize: Bus shelter exhibition in Miami.

item.title: Something Like Joy · Decagon Gallery
item.description: Online photography exhibition seeking the happiness that catches you off guard — authentic, unposed moments of joy, beauty, and delight found in ordinary life rather than staged celebrations. Selected work is shown in a curated online exhibition with dedicated pages, Instagram features, and a printed catalog. Open to photographers worldwide. Submit up to 4 images. First place receives $500 plus a solo website feature; second $250; third $150; two honorable mentions $50 each — $1,000 total cash awards. — Deadline: September 15, 2026. Fee: $25 (4 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: $1,000 total.

item.title: Motion > Blur · Praxis Photo Arts Center
item.description: Juried exhibition at Praxis Gallery in Minneapolis exploring how blur conveys velocity, gesture, and emotional tone — capturing movement within still photography to introduce surreal, kinetic qualities. All genres and processes welcome. Up to 38 images are selected for the physical gallery show (August 22 – September 12, 2026). Awards include Directors' Choice (free entry into two future calls) and five honorable mentions featured in the exhibition, printed catalog, and online gallery. Images shown at Praxis within the past year are ineligible; Praxis members get 10 images for the price of 5. — Deadline: July 19, 2026. Fee: $35 (5 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Glasgow Photography Zine · Glasgow Gallery of Photography
item.description: The Glasgow Gallery of Photography invites photographers worldwide to submit work for a forthcoming zine celebrating Glasgow — its people, streets, architecture, music, communities, weather, industry, nightlife, green spaces, rituals, and everyday moments. Work must relate to or have been made in Glasgow, but photographers need not be Glaswegian. All styles and processes are welcome, including digital, analogue, documentary, conceptual, portraiture, landscape, street, and experimental. Submit up to five images, individually or as a short series; selected work appears in the printed zine (£10 to buy), promoted across the gallery's social media and network. Free to submit. — Deadline: July 24, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: FORMAT27 Open Call — PLAY
item.description: The FORMAT International Photography Festival in Derby, UK, invites exhibition and event proposals worldwide for its 2027 biennale on the theme 'PLAY' — experimentation, improvisation, and rule-breaking, from fun and exploration to questions of authorship and the politics of images. Open to artists, collectives, and curators working across documentary, multimedia, VR, moving image, installation, publications, performance, and participatory projects. Up to five projects are selected from around 250 shortlisted entries by FORMAT curators and an international jury. Selected artists exhibit at FORMAT27 (March 11 – April 11, 2027), receive a £1,000 artist fee plus up to £300 travel and accommodation during the launch weekend, and join a London group show at Photofusion Gallery in May 2027. Additional awards include a £2,500 production grant, a £1,000 printing credit, and exhibition opportunities at the Glaz (France) and Lishui (China) festivals. — Deadline: September 6, 2026. Fee: €22 early / €27 standard. Prize: £1,000 artist fee + Exhibition + £2,500 grant.

item.title: Suboart Magazine — August & September 2026 Issues
item.description: Independent print magazine based in Lisbon seeking emerging visual artists for its August and September 2026 print issues, featuring in-depth interviews, Q&As, and features. Photography, painting, sculpture, textile art, collage, and illustration welcome. Submit up to 6 works; free to apply, with a €30 fee only if accepted. Selected artists receive a free digital copy of the issue. — Deadline: July 13, 2026. Fee: Free (€30 if accepted). Prize: Publication.

item.title: Through the Lens Photography 2026 · The Joe Center for the Arts
item.description: Juried photography exhibition at The Joe Center for the Arts, a community non-profit art center in Port St. Joe, Florida, on view August 7 – September 11, 2026. Open to all photographers; all photo-based works are eligible with no limit on subject matter or technique. Submit up to 5 pieces, all priced for sale (the gallery takes a 40% commission). Cash awards include Best of Show ($200), First ($150), Second ($100), Third ($75), Honorable Mentions, and a $75 People's Choice. Accepted work must be delivered or shipped framed and ready to hang. — Deadline: July 12, 2026. Fee: $50 ($35 members). Prize: $200 / $150 / $100 / $75 + Exhibition.

item.title: 19th Fòrum Fotogràfic Can Basté
item.description: The 19th edition of the Fòrum Fotogràfic Can Basté (FFCB), a Barcelona photography forum run since 1996 by the Can Basté civic centre in the Nou Barris district. Held November 24–28, 2026 under the theme 'Retornar a les utopies' (Return to Utopias), the forum awards two kinds of free-to-enter, open-theme production grants. Three exhibition production grants of €2,000 each fund new photographic projects, with the winning works shown individually at the Sala Cava for at least 45 days between 2027 and 2028. A separate €3,000 photographic publication grant funds a photobook, edited and distributed by Ediciones Posibles. Finalists present their projects before a professional jury during the festival. Open to emerging photographic artists and collectives resident in Spain; any format or photographic technique is welcome, provided the project has not been previously exhibited or published in full. — Deadline: September 21, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: 3 × €2,000 + €3,000 photobook + exhibition.

item.title: Solstitium: Incandescent — Summer Solstice Exhibition · Griffin Museum of Photography
item.description: Free, global open call for an online group exhibition in the Griffin Museum's Virtual Gallery, marking the summer solstice. The theme is light itself — its beauty and mythology, and how it helps us reflect on the cycles of nature and life. The museum seeks photographs that treat light as the primary subject rather than incidental: delicate, dynamic, and intentional. Juror: Crista Dix, Executive Director of the Griffin Museum of Photography. Selected works are exhibited online July 15–31, 2026. Open worldwide. — Deadline: July 10, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: Dog Days of Summer · Griffin Museum of Photography
item.description: Free, global open call for an online group exhibition presented by the Griffin Museum of Photography, exploring the place dogs hold in our lives — as companions, workers, protectors, muses, and family members. The museum welcomes photographs that celebrate, question, or reveal the complex relationship between humans and dogs, from photographers of all backgrounds and experience levels. Juror: Crista Dix, Executive Director of the Griffin Museum of Photography. Selected works are exhibited online August 1–30, 2026. — Deadline: July 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: strands of silver · midwest nice art
item.description: Juried online exhibition from midwest nice art, the Sioux Falls artist-run project, exploring the beauty, complexity, and inevitability of time. The brief invites work on aging, memory, transformation, impermanence, and the spaces between beginnings and endings — from the wonder of childhood to the reflection of later years, a cherished memory or a fading photograph. All media and styles are welcome, including photography. Open to artists worldwide. — Deadline: September 20, 2026. Fee: $5. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Photo of the Season — You Can't Be Serious · The Image Flow
item.description: Seasonal photography competition from The Image Flow gallery, this cycle embracing the off-kilter. Theme: You Can't Be Serious — unique styles, questionable decisions, and conflicting emotions. Open worldwide. First prize $150, second $100, third $50, plus two honorable mentions. Winners are featured on the gallery website, newsletter, and social media, and selected images join a 2027 group exhibition at The Image Flow. Accepts film, digital, alternative process, and printmaking; AI-generated images, mixed media, and film/video are excluded. — Deadline: September 21, 2026. Fee: $15. Prize: $150 / $100 / $50 + exhibition.

item.title: FUJIFILM GFX Challenge Grant Program 2026
item.description: Global grant program supporting image-makers to realize a personal project. Fifteen recipients are selected: 5 Global Grants of $10,000 and 10 Regional Grants of $5,000. Awardees also receive a complimentary loan of a GFX System camera body (including the new GFX ETERNA 55) and two GF lenses for the duration of their project, plus mentoring and technical support from Fujifilm experts. Projects may be realized as still photography or in a movie format. Open to both amateur and professional photographers and videographers resident in eligible countries; proposals submitted in English. Free to enter, no purchase necessary. — Deadline: August 17, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $10,000 ×5 + $5,000 ×10.

item.title: Lenscratch Still Life Exhibition
item.description: Online juried exhibition dedicated to the art of still life, juried by photographer Kimberly Witham. Open to work across the genre — constructed tableaux, studies of everyday objects, and contemporary images exploring memory, symbolism, identity, and place through the language of still life. Submit one image (72dpi, 1000px long side). — Deadline: July 19, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: The Shape of a Father · L.A. Photo Curator
item.description: Open call juried by Laurie Freitag, founder of L.A. Photo Curator, exploring fatherhood in all its forms — biological parents, mentors, father figures, absence, memory, or lasting influence. A father does not need to appear in the photograph. First place receives a solo online exhibition, a featured Q&A article, and a homepage feature for one month. All selected photographers appear in a group online exhibition with artist statement and bio, with consideration for Top 40 Images of the Year and Photographer of the Year. 5% of entry fees donated to No Kid Hungry; an additional 5% to the winner's chosen charity. Submit 3 or 6 images (not 4 or 5). Limited fee waivers available on request. Open worldwide. — Deadline: July 26, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: Solo online exhibition.

item.title: Dek Unu Magazine — Tuŝis: Altered States (Annual Contest 2026)
item.description: Dek Unu Magazine's annual juried contest for adventurous, hand-made, light-and-lens-based fine art photography — photo-montage, alternative processes, hybrids, and experimental departures. Photo-hybrids that combine digital painting, original photography, and AI components are welcome as long as the work stays light-and-lens based; exclusively algorithmic or machine-made images are excluded. The jurors' top selection wins $250; all other winners have their entry fees refunded. Winners are published in the August 2026 paperback and e-reader edition of Dek Unu Magazine, showcased online for 31 days with promotion, and given a permanent permalinked catalog page. Submit 5 images. Open worldwide. — Deadline: July 15, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: $250 + magazine publication.

item.title: CitiesToBe Photo Award 2026
item.description: Third edition of the urban photography award organised by Barcelona innovation studio Anteverti — and the first to be thematic and to reward photographic series rather than single images. The 2026 theme is 'Third Places': the informal, shared spaces beyond home and work where city life unfolds. Open worldwide to anyone 18 or over, individuals or collectives, working in lens-based photography only; each participant submits one project of 10 to 20 images shot after 1 January 2024. The winner receives an acquisitive prize of €1,500 and five finalists €500 each, with selected work shown through CitiesToBe's channels and edition book. Jury: Roger Grasas, Arianna Rinaldo, Cristina Garrido, Pilar Conesa and Sergio García i Rodríguez. AI-generated or synthetic images are not eligible. Call opens 22 June, closes 30 September 2026, winners announced November 2026. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €1,500 + 5 finalists €500 each.

item.title: VI Barcelona Human Rights International Photo Festival
item.description: Sixth edition of the international photography festival on human rights and global justice organised in Barcelona by the Más Retina association. Photographers, professional or amateur, of any nationality and of legal age submit a documentary project of 15 images (at least seven made in 2025–2026) addressing social, climate, gender or economic justice. Ten projects selected by the jury are printed in large format and exhibited outdoors across Barcelona's districts during the festival. The grand prize is €3,000, with €400 for each category winner. Submission via Picter with a €5 fee per project; deadline 9 October 2026. — Deadline: October 9, 2026. Fee: €5. Prize: €3,000 + €400 per category.

item.title: HCP Annual Fellowship Awards 2026 · Houston Center for Photography
item.description: Houston Center for Photography's annual fellowship awards two photographers from anywhere in the world $3,000 each plus a solo exhibition at HCP, opening November 2026. A single juror selects two distinct awards: the Carol Crow Fellowship, for photographers advocating for the environment and celebrating natural landscapes, and the HCP Fellowship, which carries no assigned theme and recognizes work offering insight into current themes, technologies, and practices in photography. Open to all photographic, film, video, and lens-based installation work. The 2026 juror is Natasha Egan, Executive Director of the Museum of Contemporary Photography at Columbia College Chicago. There is no entry fee, but applicants must hold an HCP Fellowship membership ($35). HCP covers ground shipping for selected artists. — Deadline: July 19, 2026. Fee: $35 membership. Prize: $3,000 + Solo exhibition.

item.title: Bath Open Art Prize 2026 · Fringe Arts Bath
item.description: Now in its 14th year, the Bath Open Art Prize is an international open call run by the volunteer-led non-profit Fringe Arts Bath. Open to visual artists at any stage of their career from across the globe, it accepts work across all genres and mediums — including photography, video, painting, textile, digital, print and 3D, plus small installations and performance. Works selected by 2026 judges Simbah Pilé and Jemma Hickman are shown at 44AD artspace in Bath, UK, 16–31 October 2026. Prizes: £750 first, £250 second, £50 People's Choice art vouchers, and a 44AD solo exhibition opportunity. Entry fees (£22 for one work, £33 for up to three) help fund FaB's free annual visual arts festival. — Deadline: September 13, 2026. Fee: £22–£33. Prize: £750 + £250 + Solo exhibition.

item.title: Real And Wild — RAW Photography Awards 2026
item.description: Inaugural edition of RAW, a nature photography award built around a single rule: every image must be made within 100 km of the photographer's home — 'the wild is not far away.' Five categories: RAW Neighbors (no human elements), Coexistence (human presence), Connection (people and nature), Macro (the small world) and Perspective (the big scene). The Real And Wild Photographer of the Year receives $1,000, with $250 for each category winner; winning and shortlisted images are published in the online RAW Winners Gallery and a photo book, and promoted through a partnership with Atlantic Geographic. Blind judging by professionals. Open worldwide, with a free RAW Junior tier for under-18s. Fees: $10 for one image, $25 for five, $40 for ten. AI-generated or AI-composited images are not permitted. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: $10–$40. Prize: $1,000 grand prize + $250 per category + Photobook.
